core_settings.name: core_attributes.sensor_id
core_settings.label: Managing sensor
core_settings.description: Sensor that talks to the Cloudflare API (api.cloudflare.com, HTTPS 443) on behalf of this connector.

config_settings.name: config_attributes.zoneId
config_settings.label: Cloudflare Zone ID
config_settings.description: 32-character Zone ID of the Cloudflare zone whose custom certificates this connector manages (Cloudflare dashboard > zone Overview > API section). One connector per zone.

config_settings.name: config_attributes.authentication_method
config_settings.label: authentication_method
config_settings.description: How the Cloudflare API token is supplied: typed directly into TLM, or resolved at runtime from an external Secrets Manager (PAM) connector.

config_settings.name: config_attributes.password
config_settings.label: Cloudflare API token
config_settings.description: API token (My Profile > API Tokens) with Zone > SSL and Certificates > Edit and Zone > Zone > Read on this zone (SSL and Certificates > Edit also covers certificate packs and the Universal SSL setting). Sent as Authorization: Bearer; never logged.

config_settings.name: config_attributes.pam_connector_id
config_settings.label: secrets_manager_connector
config_settings.description: Registered Secrets Manager (PAM) connector that resolves the Cloudflare API token at runtime.

conditional_banners.title: Note
conditional_banners.description: Use the format systemName slash accountName to reference the Cloudflare API token from BeyondTrust vaults

conditional_banners.title: Note
conditional_banners.description: Use the object or secret name to reference the Cloudflare API token from CyberArk vaults

conditional_banners.title: Note
conditional_banners.description: Use the numeric secret id optionally followed by slash field slug to reference the Cloudflare API token from Delinea secrets

config_settings.name: config_attributes.password
config_settings.label: Cloudflare API token (PAM vault reference)
config_settings.description: Enter the PAM vault reference that holds the Cloudflare API token, not the token itself. BeyondTrust: SystemName/AccountName. CyberArk: object name. Delinea: secretId or secretId/fieldSlug.

config_settings.name: config_attributes.csrMode
config_settings.label: Private key and CSR generation
config_settings.description: 'Cloudflare' (default): the key pair and CSR are generated by Cloudflare (POST /custom_csrs); the private key never leaves Cloudflare and the certificate is uploaded by CSR id. Cloudflare supports RSA 2048 and ECDSA P-256 only. 'Sensor': the key pair and CSR are generated on the TLM sensor (any key size) and the private key is uploaded together with the certificate.

options.label: Cloudflare generates the key and CSR (default)
TLM sensor generates the key and CSR

config_settings.name: config_attributes.csrSubjectFallback
config_settings.label: CSR subject fallback (C, ST, L, O)
config_settings.description: Cloudflare-generated CSRs require country, state, locality and organization. Values from the TLM certificate profile's subject DN are used first; this fallback fills in any that are missing. Format: C=US, ST=Utah, L=Lehi, O=Example Inc.

config_settings.name: config_attributes.renewalStrategy
config_settings.label: How a renewed certificate replaces the existing one
config_settings.description: 'Update' (default) PATCHes the existing Cloudflare custom certificate with the renewed one in a single call (Cloudflare replaces the record and assigns it a new id). 'Upload new, delete replaced' uploads a new custom certificate and then deletes the one it replaces (the behaviour of the DigiCert post-enrollment scripts). 'Upload new, keep replaced' leaves the previous certificate in the zone for manual clean-up.

options.label: Update the existing certificate via PATCH (default)
Upload new certificate, delete the replaced one
Upload new certificate, keep the replaced one

config_settings.name: config_attributes.certificateType
config_settings.label: Certificate type for new uploads
config_settings.description: Cloudflare custom certificate type used when a NEW certificate is uploaded. 'SNI Custom' (Custom Modern, default) requires SNI-capable clients; 'Legacy Custom' also serves non-SNI clients (Business/Enterprise with legacy support). An update in place keeps the existing certificate's type.

config_settings.name: config_attributes.bundleMethod
config_settings.label: Chain bundling
config_settings.description: 'User defined' (force, default) uploads the end-entity certificate followed by the issuing CA exactly as TLM issued it and works with private CAs. 'Compatible' (ubiquitous) and 'Modern' (optimal) upload the end-entity certificate only and let Cloudflare build the chain from publicly trusted CAs.

options.label: User defined: leaf + issuing CA as issued (default)

config_settings.name: config_attributes.managedCertificates
config_settings.label: Cloudflare-managed certificates (Universal SSL / Advanced)
config_settings.description: Whether certificates Cloudflare issued itself (Universal SSL and Advanced Certificate Manager packs, e.g. from Google Trust Services or Let's Encrypt) are listed as assets so they can be replaced by a custom (DigiCert) certificate, and what happens to them afterwards. 'Discover, keep' (default) lists them and leaves them in place after the switch: Cloudflare serves the custom certificate for every hostname both cover, the managed one stays as fallback. 'Discover, retire' additionally disables Universal SSL / deletes the Advanced pack once the custom certificate is active and covers every hostname of the managed certificate. 'Ignore' lists custom certificates only.

options.label: Discover, keep as fallback after the switch (default)
Discover, retire after the switch (disable Universal SSL / delete pack)

config_settings.name: config_attributes.csrRetention
config_settings.label: Cloudflare CSRs to keep per common name
config_settings.description: After a successful install in Cloudflare CSR mode, older Cloudflare CSR records with the same common name are deleted, keeping this many most recent ones (the CSR just used is always kept). 0 keeps only the current CSR.
